headline: The gold leaves out the customer's own card-number lookup, but the agent cannot get the card's last 4 digits without it, so every correct trajectory leaves an extra DB row and fails.

issues.summary: The gold gives the user get_card_last_4_digits (gold[13]) and files the dispute with card_last_4_digits '2791' (gold[15]), but it never replays the user's call_discoverable_user_tool lookup. That lookup writes a row to user_discoverable_tool_calls and is the only way to obtain '2791'.
evidence: user instructions: "(If the agent provides you with the get_card_last_4_digits tool, use it to retrieve the number.)"
gold[15].arguments: "card_last_4_digits": "2791"; no user-requestor action in the gold
get_credit_card_accounts_by_user returns no last-4 field (db.json credit_card_accounts.cc_e9d195fe8e_silver has none)

Replay: gold + user call_discoverable_user_tool(get_card_last_4_digits, cc_e9d195fe8e_silver) -> returns 'Last 4 digits of card: 2791'; verified match False (user_discoverable_tool_calls only_pred 9a452d6c48d8d07e)
contrast task_041 gold[4-7], which do include the user's get_card_last_4_digits calls
issues.why_it_matters: A trajectory where the user does not look up the number cannot supply '2791', so the dispute record differs. A trajectory where the user does look it up leaves a row the gold lacks. No path matches the gold under either the exact or the verified scorer.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a user action call_discoverable_user_tool {discoverable_tool_name: get_card_last_4_digits, arguments: {"credit_card_account_id": "cc_e9d195fe8e_silver"}} between gold[13] and gold[15].

issues.summary: The gold processes the CLI before filing the dispute, so the approval passes the 'no pending disputes' check. No doc says to sequence a concurrent CLI ahead of a dispute, and the customer raises the dispute first.
evidence: user instructions: "State BOTH requests upfront, but the dispute first"
doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_007 Step 2: "3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes."
tools.py approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 returns 'cannot be approved' when any user dispute has status SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW/PENDING
gold order: CLI submit/approve gold[10],[12] before dispute gold[15]
task notes (not agent-visible): "process the CLI FIRST before filing the dispute"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that handles the dispute first, in the customer's order, then correctly denies the CLI for pending_disputes, producing a different credit_limit and CLI records. Reordering to avoid an eligibility rule is a judgment call the docs neither require nor endorse.
issues.suggested_fix: Add guidance to logistics_007 for concurrent dispute and CLI requests (e.g. 'when a customer requests both, complete the CLI first'), or have the customer ask for the CLI first.

issues.summary: The internal CLI workflow doc that 'MUST be followed in the exact order' has an empty Step 3 (payment history and amount check). The payment-history rule and the get_payment_history_6183 tool are only described in a separate doc.
evidence:
doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_007: "## Step 3: Verify Payment History and Requested Amount

.

## Step 4"
doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_007: "These steps MUST be followed in the exact order listed."

doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_006: "Use the get_payment_history_6183 tool to verify the customer's payment history meets the requirement for their card tier." (the only doc naming the tool)
issues.why_it_matters: get_payment_history_6183 is a gold-required read, so its tool name must appear in agent_discoverable_tools. An agent that follows only the step-by-step workflow doc finds no instruction to call it. Doc 006 is in required_documents and says to call it, so a careful agent still reaches the gold.
issues.suggested_fix: Fill Step 3 of logistics_007 with the payment-history check (call get_payment_history_6183 with the tier's month count) and the per-tier maximum-increase check from logistics_006.

solution_check: CLI: Silver Rewards is mid tier (90 days, 80%, 3 months, 50% max). The card was opened 11/15/2024 with utilization 4500/15000 = 30%, no CLI history, and on-time payments, so a $7,500 increase to $22,500 is approved. Dispute: TechDirect $1,247.99 on 10/10/2025, goods_services_not_received, more than 30 days old, merchant contacted, no prior disputes, under the $5000 mid-tier cap, so provisional credit is true and issue_noticed_date is 10/31/2025. These values match the gold, but the gold DB omits the user lookup row needed to get '2791'.
prior_note: The prior review found it clean. It did not report the missing user lookup action or the undocumented CLI-before-dispute sequencing.
notes: gold[13] and gold[15] have compare_args set, but reward_basis is DB only, so ACTION matching does not apply. The fixture payment_history includes ph_e9d195fe8e_silver_006 dated 2025-11-15, after the fixed date 11/14/2025. It is cosmetic (all ON_TIME). The approval record collides with the submit record id (both seed '7500.00'), so only the PENDING record persists, the same quirk as task_050.
